title: Maximum Throughput

story.briefing: Every approved window still needs a channel. How many channels does the Core need so that no two simultaneous windows ever share one?
story.success: Channel count settled. Nothing collides, and nothing is wasted.

description: Given a list of windows, each a two-element array [start, end] with start strictly less than end, return the smallest number of channels needed so that no channel ever carries two windows at the same moment. A window ending exactly when another begins may reuse the same channel. An empty list returns 0.

examples.explanation: The first two overlap; the third reuses a channel.

hints: The answer is the largest number of windows that are ever open at the same instant. You never need more channels than that, and never fewer.
You do not need to know which windows overlap — only how many are open at once. Treat each start and each end as a separate event on a timeline.

Make a list of starts and a list of ends, both sorted. Sweep them together, adding a channel on each start and releasing one on each end, and record the highest count reached. Process an end before a start at the same instant.
